tagline: A miners' road over Barlow Pass, gravel in the middle.
intro: The byway begins at Granite Falls, but the line drawn here starts a few miles short of Verlot and follows the South Fork Stillaguamish River upstream past Verlot and Silverton and under Big Four Mountain to Barlow Pass, at 2,349 feet. There the pavement quits. The road turns north as gravel Forest Road 20 and follows the Sauk River down past Bedal, picking up pavement again at the Whitechuck bridge into Darrington.

Miners pushed the way through in 1891, when the surveyor M.Q. Barlow blazed a route from Silverton toward the strikes at Monte Cristo, and a railroad started up the same line the next year. Loggers and the CCC made a road of it later. The tracks are gone.

moments.title: Verlot
moments.text: Civilian Conservation Corps crews put up the ranger buildings here between 1933 and 1942, and the Forest Service still opens them in season to help plan an outing.

moments.title: Big Four Ice Caves
moments.text: Avalanche snow piles up under the mountain's 4,200-foot north face and can last all year in its shade, and hikers are told to stay out of the caves that melt into it.

moments.title: Monte Cristo
moments.text: Four miles beyond Barlow Pass, on a road closed to motor vehicles, the town that started it all mined gold and silver from 1889 to 1907, then carried on as a resort until 1983.

practical: The middle section north of Barlow Pass is single-lane gravel, and snow lingering at Barlow Pass usually limits the full drive to late spring through fall.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Mountain Loop Scenic Byway
